key_insight: Instead of only making a language model think longer or use deeper layers, Latent Lattice Language Models increase the number of computational states it maintains. A lattice of latent streams carries information across both token positions and network depth.
problem_solved: The paper explores how to expand language-model computational capacity beyond deeper layers, repeated computation, or extra latent reasoning steps.
method: Introduce a Lattice of Latents: horizontal latent streams maintained at each layer.
Run these latent streams recurrently across token positions to carry state through time.
Combine horizontal streams with the vertical residual stream that carries information through network depth.
impact: This offers practitioners an architectural direction for increasing model capacity through persistent computational states. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so performance gains and computational trade-offs cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: A grid diagram with token positions on the horizontal axis and network layers on the vertical axis.
Color-coded arrows distinguishing horizontal recurrent streams from vertical residual flow.
A side-by-side schematic comparing a conventional residual stack with the latent lattice.
A concept panel contrasting deeper computation, repeated computation, and more maintained states.
paper_authors: Shivam Duggal, Zongze Wu, William T. Freeman, Antonio Torralba, Richard Zhang
